headline: A 43-year-old man in primary prevention with a 7-year pattern of Stage-1-range blood pressure, a single 2022 hypertension diagnosis that was diagnosed, treated for one day on paper, declined, and then never carried forward, worsening lipids (HDL falling 52->40, TG 282, chol/HDL ratio 3.1->4.7), creeping weight (174->187 lb), and a heavy bilateral family history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and early MI. His modifiable cardiovascular risk is real and drifting upward, yet the chart treats him as a healthy young man: hypertension is absent from the problem list, no statin or antihypertensive is active, the chart never calculated an ASCVD risk (this analysis computes it: 10-yr ASCVD 1.06%->2.04%, rising, every input recoverable from the export including race), and two external 2024 emergency cardiovascular work-ups never re-entered the primary-care narrative.

findings.claim: Hypertension was formally diagnosed and pharmacologically treated on 8/29/2022, then was never re-coded, never added to the problem list, and never re-addressed at any later visit — it now exists in the chart only as readings, a one-day encounter diagnosis, and a declined prescription.
findings.significance: Because 'Primary hypertension' is NOT on the structured problem list (the list holds only GERD, post-concussion syndrome, resolved neck pain, and two allergy diagnoses), it will not surface in problem-list-driven views, registry/quality measures, or any ASCVD risk calculator that reads the problem list. A clinician scanning the chart sees a healthy 43-year-old. The condition is real but invisible to the systems meant to act on it. This is the single most consequential gap in his cardiovascular care.

The patient himself reported at the 2022 visit that his 'blood pressure typically in the upper 130s for the past 10 years,' so the office readings agree with his own home data. Untreated Stage 1 HTN in a 43-year-old is a decades-long cumulative exposure.

findings.claim: The lipid panel is deteriorating across the three available draws: total cholesterol 159->156->188, HDL 52->44->40 (now flagged Low), total/HDL ratio 3.1->3.5->4.7, and triglycerides 88->92->282 (flagged High) with VLDL 56 (flagged High). The 12/4/2025 panel is the first to carry multiple abnormal flags. LDL has stayed near-stable (89->94->92).
findings.significance: An atherogenic shift: the protective HDL is falling while the ratio and triglycerides climb — a metabolic-syndrome-type pattern that tracks with the 13-lb weight gain and is exactly the lipid signature that adds to ASCVD risk beyond LDL alone. The 282 triglyceride and 188 total cholesterol on 12/4/2025 were drawn NON-FASTING lab comment: 'PATIENT WAS NOT FASTING', which inflates triglycerides and the calculated VLDL/ratio — so the true fasting numbers may be milder, but the multi-year HDL decline and ratio rise are not fasting-dependent and are real. A fasting redraw is needed to act on the triglycerides, but the trend already warrants attention.

findings.claim: No global ASCVD/PREVENT risk has been computed anywhere in the record, and no lipid-lowering or antiplatelet therapy has ever been ordered — the entire medication history contains no statin, fibrate, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitor, aspirin, or any antihypertensive other than the declined lisinopril.
findings.significance: Risk is being managed reading-by-reading and lab-by-lab rather than as an integrated estimate. For a 43-year-old man the 10-year ASCVD number is likely still low, but he has the inputs that drive 30-year / lifetime risk (sustained Stage-1 BP, falling HDL, family loading, overweight) — precisely the patient in whom guidelines favor risk-enhancer-informed discussion and early lifestyle/statin consideration. The chart never frames the question, so the opportunity for early primary prevention is going unaddressed by default rather than by an explicit, documented decision.

Whether the grandparents' events were premature (the ASCVD-relevant cut: MI/stroke <55 male / <65 female) is unknown — the age of onset is not recorded for every family-history row — but the density of vascular disease across both lineages is itself a reason to treat his modifiable factors more aggressively, not less.

No evidence of vertebral dissection,' <50% ICA stenosis bilaterally) plus IV fluids. Neither has a clinic note, and the 7/2/2024 PCP visit (six weeks after the chest pain) makes no mention of it.
findings.significance: Two pieces of genuinely reassuring cardiovascular data — a negative troponin and a clean neck CTA showing no atherosclerosis at 41-42 — are sitting in the chart unintegrated. They argue AGAINST established disease (good news the risk discussion should use), but because they live only as imported external orders with the narrative buried inside the radiology narrative and no reconciliation note, the PCP storyline never acknowledges that the patient had chest pain or a dissection scare at all. The chest pain was attributed in the radiology indication to cannabis ('Chest pain since yesterday after consuming THC') — a context worth carrying forward given his documented occasional cannabis use. The discrete lab values did not survive the import (CMP/troponin resulted as order headers only), so only the abnormal/normal flags and the imaging reads remain.

findings.significance: He is not diabetic and not prediabetic by A1c, so dysglycemia is not currently a driver — but the steady weight gain is the plausible common cause behind the simultaneous BP elevation, HDL decline, and triglyceride rise (a clustering toward metabolic syndrome). The fact that he independently wore a CGM signals real engagement with his own metabolic health that the visits could harness — yet the CGM was logged as 'not taking' by 12/2025 and no glucose data from it entered the structured record. Weight/lifestyle is the highest-yield, lowest-risk lever here and is the one the notes gesture at ('healthy diet and lifestyle') without a concrete plan.

findings.claim: End-organ and metabolic safety labs are reassuring: eGFR >90 at both 2022 and 2025, creatinine 0.94->0.98 (normal), potassium normal (5.0, 4.7), glucose 90-97. The only BMP flags are a trivially high CO2 (30, 2022) and a borderline BUN (21, 2025).
findings.significance: There is no renal contraindication or electrolyte barrier to an ACE inhibitor/ARB or thiazide — the declined lisinopril could have been safely restarted or substituted at any point. It also means his hypertension has not yet produced detectable kidney injury, so the window for damage-preventing treatment is still open. This is a 'nothing is stopping treatment except inertia' finding.

findings.claim: When the ASCVD-estimator inputs are assembled from the record, the 10-year risk the chart never computed is LOW but non-trivial and rising: every input — including the one input the first pass thought was missing, RACE (PATIENT_RACE_C_NAME='White', PATIENT_RACE LINE 1) — is present in this export, so the estimate does NOT need a wide race-driven spread. As a confirmed White, non-Hispanic male the Pooled Cohort Equations give a defensible 10-year ASCVD of 1.06% on the confirmed-fasting 2018 panel rising to 2.04% on the latest (2025) panel; the AHA PREVENT (2023) base model gives a concordant ~1.6%->2.4% (10-yr ASCVD) / ~1.6%->2.4% (10-yr total-CVD). The estimate has nearly DOUBLED in absolute terms on worsening-but-still-modest inputs, driven mostly by the HDL fall 52->40, not by the non-fasting cholesterol.
findings.significance: This is the number the chart should have produced and never did. It reframes the case correctly: the 10-year ASCVD figure is BELOW the 5% 'borderline' and 7.5% 'intermediate' statin-discussion thresholds, so a guideline-literal reading says 'no statin indicated today' — which is exactly why the omission has felt defensible by default. But the honest reading is the opposite: a 43-year-old whose estimate has already nearly DOUBLED (1.06%->2.04%) on worsening-but-still-modest inputs, who carries guideline risk-enhancers (family history, the falling HDL, the metabolic drift) that the equations under-weight, is the textbook candidate for a risk-enhancer-informed discussion and lifestyle intervention NOW, while the 30-year/lifetime risk is the relevant horizon. The point of computing it is not the small percentage; it is that the trajectory of the inputs is unambiguous and the conversation it should trigger has never been framed. Every input, the estimate, and the caveats are shown in the ASCVD section.

findings.claim: His blood pressure elevation is NOT white-coat: the office mean of 132 systolic is concordant with his own reported home pattern of 'upper 130s for the past 10 years,' so the in-clinic readings are corroborated by out-of-office self-report rather than contradicted by it — a comparison the record contains but never draws.
findings.significance: White-coat hypertension is the standard reason to NOT treat an office Stage-1 reading without confirmation, and it is the most plausible reason a clinician might have left this untreated. The data refute that escape hatch: the patient volunteered that he 'occasionally checks at home' and runs 'upper 130s for the past 10 years' (note:HNO_3819029543), which agrees with the 132 office mean. So the office Stage-1 classification is, in this one respect, already partially confirmed by the patient's own data — the very confirmation guidelines ask for before treating, and an argument FOR treating rather than a reason to defer. Formal home/ABPM logging is still absent and should be obtained, but the white-coat hypothesis is not supported.

findings.claim: He is untreated on BOTH modifiable lipid/BP axes simultaneously, by two different mechanisms: the one antihypertensive ever started (lisinopril) was declined and never re-attempted, and no lipid-lowering therapy was ever started despite a lipid panel that worsened across every draw — so the atherogenic shift (HDL 52->40, ratio 3.1->4.7) accrued with zero pharmacologic counter-pressure and, unlike the BP, was never even proposed.
findings.significance: These are two distinct failure modes that the record never sets side by side. The BP axis failed at the patient-adherence step (a documented decline) and was then abandoned; the lipid axis never reached a decision at all — no statin was offered, declined, or charted, even as the panel deteriorated and HDL crossed into the 'Low' flag. Stating them together shows the under-treatment is not one patient refusal but a systemic non-engagement with the whole modifiable-risk picture: one lever was tried once and dropped, the other was never picked up.

findings.significance: This is the sharpest single statement of the care pattern. Acute reactivity vs. chronic neglect is the structural signature, and the undercoding is the mechanism that perpetuates it: with HTN off the problem list, nothing prompts the chronic axis at any of those six visits, while the acute symptom always has a presenting complaint to drive a workup.

Re-running the Pooled Cohort Equations across the plausible fasting-TC range (160-188) with the measured HDL 40 holds his 10-year ASCVD in a tight 1.5-2.0% band; even if fasting reverted total cholesterol all the way to his 2018 level (159), he lands at ~1.45-1.52% — still well above the 1.06% he sat at in 2018 when HDL was 52. So the fasting caveat narrows the uncertainty on the number without changing the direction or the indicated conversation. Quantifying the redraw scenarios turns 'we should repeat it fasting' from a reason to wait into a bounded prediction of where he will still be.

findings.claim: Acute-vs-chronic mismatch, quantified: in 2024 the system fired correctly and fast for two ACUTE cardiovascular scares (5/14/2024 chest pain -> same-day negative troponin + normal CXR; 7/30/2024 suspected vertebral dissection -> clean neck CTA + IV fluids), while across the same period the CHRONIC accumulating risk was re-addressed at ZERO of the 6 PCP visits that followed the 8/29/2022 hypertension diagnosis — including all 3 visits AFTER the 9/28/2023 documented decline — despite 5 of those 6 visits carrying an at/above-Stage-1 reading. The missed-opportunity window is ~3.3 years (8/29/2022 -> 12/4/2025) and 6 contacts wide.
findings.significance: This is the structural signature of the whole case: reactive apparatus intact, proactive apparatus absent. The acute symptom always supplies a presenting complaint that drives a workup; the chronic, asymptomatic risk supplies none, and the undercoding (hypertension off the problem list) removes the only systemic prompt that could have substituted for a symptom. The 2024 negative troponin and clean CTA are genuinely reassuring data that ARGUE the chronic risk is still pre-clinical and therefore still preventable — yet they were never folded back to motivate the chronic conversation. The window is not abstract: it is six specific dated visits at which a 30-second risk discussion was available and not had.

findings.claim: The premature-CVD family-history risk enhancer cannot be confirmed or excluded from ANY source in this export — not the structured FAMILY_HX table (AGE_OF_ONSET is NULL for all 12 cardiovascular facts) and not the notes (the 'Age of Onset' column in the family-history block of every annual note, 2022/2023/2025, is printed blank). So the strongest, ASCVD-guideline-recognized form of the enhancer (first-degree MI/stroke at <55 male / <65 female) is genuinely unrecoverable and must be obtained by asking, not by deeper chart mining.
findings.significance: This is a deliberate negative finding: the deep dive went looking in the unstructured notes precisely because the structured onset ages were null, and confirmed they are absent THERE too. That closes the loop honestly — the density of vascular disease (HTN x2 first-degree, hyperlipidemia x2 first-degree, MI x2 and stroke x2 across the grandparents) is itself a recognized soft risk enhancer that argues for treating his modifiable factors more aggressively, but the hard 'premature first-degree event' criterion stays unproven. Stating where the data simply does not exist is as important as stating what it shows; it tells the next clinician exactly which one question to ask.

evidence.structured_null: FAMILY_HX: 12 CV-related rows (HTN Mother/Brother, hyperlipidemia Father/Brother, stroke x2 maternal grandparents, MI x2 paternal grandparents); AGE_OF_ONSET and AGE_OF_ONSET_END NULL on every one.
evidence.notes_blank: 8/29/2022, 9/28/2023, and 12/4/2025 annual notes each print a Family History table with an 'Age of Onset' column that is empty for every entry.
evidence.first_degree: The grandparents' MI/stroke are second-degree; the first-degree CV facts (HTN, hyperlipidemia) are not hard ASCVD events, so even with onset ages the classic 'premature first-degree MI/stroke' enhancer would not be met by the current relatives.

argument: Is this patient's cardiovascular risk understood and managed? Partly understood, and essentially not managed. The data tell a coherent story that the chart never assembles. Joshua Mandel is a 43-year-old man whose blood pressure has run in the Stage-1 hypertension range for seven years (mean systolic 132, 8/9 readings at/above threshold, his own home data agreeing), whose HDL has fallen from 52 to 40 while his cholesterol/HDL ratio climbed from 3.1 to 4.7 and triglycerides spiked to 282, who has gained 13 pounds into the overweight range, and who carries hypertension in two first-degree relatives, hyperlipidemia in two more, and a hard atherosclerotic event (stroke or MI) in all four grandparents. Each of these is a recognized, modifiable or risk-enhancing driver; together they are the textbook accumulating profile of a young man on a slow track toward atherosclerotic disease. The management story is one of a single early, correct move that then evaporated. In August 2022 the new PCP did exactly the right thing: named Stage-1 HTN, ordered a baseline BMP, and started lisinopril. But the patient never took it, it was discontinued thirteen months later as a 'Patient refusal' recorded only in the medication table, and from that point hypertension disappears from the record — never re-coded, never problem-listed, never re-raised. The three annual notes since read identically: 'discussed healthy diet and lifestyle; BP and weight good,' a boilerplate that is contradicted by the very vitals printed at the top of the same notes. No ASCVD or PREVENT risk was ever estimated in the chart — so this analysis computes it: a defensible 10-year ASCVD of 1.06%->2.04% for this confirmed White male, every input recoverable from the export, the rise driven mostly by the falling HDL. No statin, no antiplatelet, and no second antihypertensive attempt exists in the entire medication history. The renal/electrolyte labs are clean, so nothing clinical is blocking treatment — only inertia. The trajectory is the point: nothing here is acutely dangerous today (negative troponin, clean neck CTA with no atherosclerosis at 42, normal A1c, normal kidneys), but every modifiable lever is drifting the wrong way and the chart's structure actively hides that. The undercoding (Finding F1) is the mechanism of the neglect, not a clerical footnote: because HTN is not on the problem list, no problem-list-driven reminder, registry, or risk tool will ever flag him, so the omission is self-perpetuating. Meanwhile two genuinely reassuring external cardiovascular work-ups sit unreconciled, so even the good news isn't being used to frame a risk conversation. What a cardiologist would want done: (1) confirm the hypertension with home/ambulatory readings and put it on the problem list; (2) re-open the antihypertensive conversation that ended in a one-sided 'refusal,' with a documented shared decision; (3) repeat the lipids FASTING to get a true triglyceride, and carry the now-computed ASCVD estimate (1.06%->2.04%) into a risk-enhancer-informed shared decision rather than leaving the number unframed; (4) make the weight/lifestyle plan concrete and leverage his demonstrated willingness to self-monitor (the CGM); (5) fold the 2024 negative troponin and clean CTA into the record as the reassuring baseline they are. The fundamentals are favorable and the patient is engaged — but the risk is real, rising, and currently unowned.
open_questions: Are the family cardiovascular events PREMATURE (MI/stroke <55M/<65F)? The age of onset is not recorded for any family-history entry, so the strongest version of the family-history risk enhancer cannot be confirmed from the data — it needs to be asked.

What are this patient's HOME blood pressures? The 8/29/2022 note says he checks 'occasionally' and runs 'upper 130s for the past 10 years,' but no home/ambulatory readings are stored. Office Stage-1 BP should be confirmed out-of-office before (and to justify) treatment.

What did the declined lisinopril actually represent — a true informed refusal, a cost/side-effect concern, or a preference for lifestyle-first? The structured reason is a generic '* Patient refusal'; the same-day note is silent. The shared-decision content is unrecoverable from the export.

What were the discrete values of the 5/14/2024 CMP and troponin and the 7/30/2024 BMP? They resulted as 'Final result' order headers with no discrete-result rows, so only abnormal/normal flags survived the import; the actual numbers are not in the EHI extract.

Was a fasting lipid ever repeated after the non-fasting 282 triglyceride / 40 HDL on 12/4/2025? No later lab contact exists in the export (last contact 12/4/2025; a 6/16/2027 'Scheduled' encounter is excluded). The atherogenic shift is therefore unconfirmed by a fasting redraw.

Did any glucose data from the FreeStyle Libre 3 CGM (worn 3/2024-2025) enter the record? No CGM glucose values appear in the structured data; only the device orders are present, and the device was marked 'not taking' by 12/2025.
limits: Single-specimen, single-export view: only what this patient's Epic EHI export carried. External (UW) emergency data arrived as imported orders/narrative with discrete lab values stripped; no outside clinic notes are present.
Blood pressures are office readings only (9 encounters); no home/ABPM data, so the Stage-1 classification rests on in-clinic measurement.
Lipid trend rests on three draws (2018 fasting, 2023 + 2025 non-fasting); the 2025 triglyceride/VLDL/ratio are inflated by non-fasting status and need a fasting confirmation before acting.

The ASCVD risk score IS now computed: a defensible Pooled-Cohort-Equations 10-year ASCVD of 1.06%->2.04% for this confirmed White, non-Hispanic male, cross-checked against AHA PREVENT 2023. Every PCE input is present in the export — race included (the first pass wrongly believed race was missing). The residual uncertainties are bounded and stated in the caveats below (office-only BP, a non-fasting latest lipid whose effect is quantified in the fasting-redraw scenario, an eGFR resulting as '>90' so assumed 95 for PREVENT); none of them change the order of magnitude or the indicated conversation.

The premature-family-CVD enhancer remains genuinely unrecoverable: the age of onset is blank for every family-history entry and the 'Age of Onset' column is blank in every annual note, so it must be asked, not mined.

synthesis.summary: A deeper synthesis over the assembled record: (1) the 10-year ASCVD that the chart never produced, computed two independent ways with every input abstracted from the data (the ascvd object below); and (2) four comparisons the notes never state but the data supports — office BP corroborated by the patient's own home report (not white-coat), simultaneous under-treatment on both modifiable axes by two different mechanisms, the acute-vs-chronic care mismatch with the missed-opportunity window quantified, and where a fasting-confirmed lipid would land the risk. The throughline: the inputs to a real risk estimate were all present all along; only their assembly was missing.

ascvd.model: ACC/AHA 2013 Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) as the primary 10-year ASCVD estimate, with the AHA PREVENT 2023 base model as an independent, race-free cross-check. Both re-derived from their published coefficient tables and verified to reproduce the figures below; primary-prevention patient (no established ASCVD, no diabetes).

inputs.name: Race
inputs.source: structured — NOT missing (corrects the first pass)

inputs.name: Systolic BP
inputs.value: 132 mmHg — the mean of 9 office readings (range 122-142) AND, coincidentally, the latest (12/4/2025) reading; corroborated by patient home report 'upper 130s'
inputs.cite: vitals[kind=blood_pressure] (mean 132.3, n=9); note:HNO_3819029543 @ CSN 948004323 ('upper 130s for the past 10 years')

inputs.name: On BP treatment
inputs.value: No — the one antihypertensive (lisinopril) was declined and never taken

estimate.primary_model: PCE (White male, untreated, non-smoker, non-diabetic, SBP 132)
estimate.low: 1.06% 10-year ASCVD (on the confirmed-fasting 2018 panel: TC 159 / HDL 52)
estimate.high: 2.04% 10-year ASCVD (on the latest 2025 panel: TC 188 / HDL 40)
estimate.basis: PCE re-derived from the published 2013 coefficient table (White male: baseline survival 0.9144, mean linear-predictor 61.18); reproduces 1.06% / 1.28% / 2.04% across the three panels to 2 decimal places. SBP sensitivity on the 2025 panel: 1.78% at SBP 122, 2.04% at 132, 2.32% at 142.
estimate.prevent_crosscheck: AHA PREVENT 2023 base model (male, eGFR 95, SBP 132, untreated, non-DM, non-smoker): ~1.64% (2018) -> 2.37% (2025) 10-year ASCVD — concordant with PCE and requiring no race input, which independently confirms the White-coefficient PCE read.
estimate.interpretation: Below the 5% borderline and 7.5% intermediate statin-discussion thresholds today, so guideline-literal = 'no statin indicated now.' But the estimate has nearly DOUBLED in absolute terms (1.06% -> 2.04%) on still-modest inputs, the rise driven mostly by the falling HDL, and the equations under-weight his risk enhancers (bilateral family CV loading, metabolic drift) and his 30-year/lifetime horizon. The number's value is the trajectory and the conversation it should trigger, not the small percentage.

caveats: RACE is confirmed (White), so — unlike the first pass — there is NO wide race-driven spread; the discarded African-American-coefficient figures (3.6-4.1%) do not apply and were an artifact of a false 'race unknown' assumption.

BP is OFFICE-ONLY (9 encounters; no logged home/ABPM). It is corroborated by the patient's own home report of 'upper 130s', so it is not over-read, but formal out-of-office confirmation is still absent.

The latest (2025) lipid was NON-FASTING (TG 282, TC 188). The non-fasting status can inflate TC, so the 2.04% upper bound is, if anything, slightly high — but HDL 40 is directly measured and fasting-independent, so a fasting redraw still lands him ~1.5-2.0%; the atherogenic shift is real regardless.
eGFR resulted as '>90' with no discrete value, so PREVENT uses an assumed 95; the true value only moves PREVENT trivially at this level.
PCE is validated for ages 40-79; 43 is in range. The 2018 estimate at age 35 is shown for trajectory only (below the validated floor) and is not a clinical figure.
LDL is not an explicit PCE input; the LDL has stayed near-stable (89->94->92) and does not drive the change — the HDL does.
ascvd.src: Computed from dataset.json inputs cited per-input above; PCE/PREVENT coefficients from the published equations (ACC/AHA 2013; Khan et al. Circulation 2024). Re-derivation reproduces the stated figures.

comparisons.statement: Office mean systolic 132 is CONCORDANT with the patient's own home report 'upper 130s for the past 10 years' => corroborated sustained hypertension, NOT white-coat. The chart holds both numbers but never sets them side by side.

Untreated on BOTH modifiable axes by two different mechanisms: BP reached a decision and failed at adherence (lisinopril declined); lipids never reached a decision at all (no statin ever offered) even as the panel worsened to HDL 40 Low.

Acute apparatus fired correctly in 2024 (negative troponin, clean neck CTA) while chronic risk was re-addressed at 0 of 6 PCP visits after the 8/29/2022 dx (3 after the 9/28/2023 decline); 5 of those 6 readings were at/above Stage 1; the missed window is ~3.3 years.

A fasting redraw cannot rescue the picture: with the directly-measured HDL 40 held fixed, PCE stays 1.5-2.0% across the plausible fasting-TC range (160-188); even reverting TC to the 2018 value (159) gives 1.52% vs the 1.06% he had at HDL 52. The driver is the HDL fall, which is fasting-independent.

abstracted_from_notes: Home BP self-report 'blood pressure typically in the upper 130s for the past 10 years' and 'occasionally checks at home' (note:HNO_3819029543, 8/29/2022) — the out-of-office corroboration that refutes white-coat (F14).

Explicit BP-pharmacotherapy offer 'Discussed medication options including amitriptyline and BP medication' (note:HNO_3819029543) — shows the lever was raised, making later silence a discontinuation of attention (F15).

Premature-CVD onset ages: confirmed ABSENT in the notes too — the 'Age of Onset' column in the family-history block of every annual note (2022/2023/2025) is printed blank, matching the null FAMILY_HX.AGE_OF_ONSET; the enhancer must be asked, not mined (F18).

Race/ethnicity for the ASCVD model: not stated in the notes (which give only 'originally from Massachusetts', 'works for Microsoft'), but recovered from the STRUCTURED tables (PATIENT_RACE='White', ETHNIC_GROUP='Not Hispanic or Latino') — correcting the first pass's belief that race was missing.
Non-fasting status of the 2025 lipid ('PATIENT WAS NOT FASTING') and fasting status of the 2018 panel ('PATIENT FASTING'), read from the lab comment text, to bound the fasting-redraw scenario (F16).
Occasional-cannabis context and the THC-attributed chest pain ('Chest pain since yesterday after consuming THC', radiology indication) — supports the benign read of the 2024 acute scare (F7/F17).

narrative.text: Hypertension diagnosed and treated once in 8/2022, then declined and never carried forward; absent from the problem list.
Stage-1-range BP for 7 years (mean systolic 132, 8/9 readings >=130/80).
Atherogenic lipid drift: HDL 52->40, chol/HDL 3.1->4.7, TG to 282 (non-fasting).
Heavy bilateral CV family history; two external 2024 CV work-ups (negative troponin, clean neck CTA) never reconciled into the PCP record.
